title: Test your replication basics
guideLabel: Re-read the types at a glance

questions.q: Someone deletes the wrong rows by mistake. Your database has a live replica. What happens to the replica?
options: It keeps the rows, so you can restore them
It copies the delete too, mistake included
It refuses changes it cannot verify
It pauses until a person approves
questions.explain: A replica copies your mistakes too, which is why replication is not a backup. A backup is a point-in-time copy you restore from, so you will usually want both.

questions.q: A shop's database says "order saved" first and sends the copy to a far-away server a moment later. If the main server dies right then, what can happen?
options: The copy wipes all of its older orders
The copy refuses to take over at all
Every earlier order is lost for good
The very last orders may be missing
questions.explain: That is asynchronous replication: fast, but a bit behind. The copy is made after the save is confirmed, so a crash can lose the last few changes.

questions.q: A tool copies only the rows that are newer than its last run. Which kind of change will it never notice?
options: A row that was deleted
A row that was added
A row that was edited
A brand new table
questions.explain: A deleted row is no longer there to be found, so key-based copying misses it. Reading the database's change log is the most complete way, because it records every insert, update and delete.

questions.q: Which direction of data flow does the post suggest for almost every case?
options: Two-way, so both sites stay equal
One-way, from a main copy to the others
Many-way, for the most safety
Whatever the database brand prefers
questions.explain: One-way is the calmer choice for almost every case. Two-way is only for when two sites must both accept writes, and it needs a plan for who wins a conflict.

questions.q: You send a weekly report from a small table that rarely changes. What is usually enough?
options: A two-way setup between two servers
A log reader running all day
A simple snapshot copy now and then
A synchronous copy of every write
questions.explain: Snapshots suit small tables that rarely change, like a list of country codes. A nightly export is enough for some jobs, so match the setup to the job.
